From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: model-fit probe & parity checklist — Veridian

Hi Jen — great to meet today, thanks for walking us through the Veridian use case (agent-assisted claims intake + triage). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a short model-fit probe: 

Summary of call
- Primary goal: replace the existing proprietary LLM call for initial triage while keeping false positive triage at <4% and intent recall >92%.
- Typical input: short support narratives (~30–120 tokens), with 10–15% of requests containing tables / pasted logs.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for the triage call in production.

Recommended probe plan (2 weeks):
1) Models to trial (suggested order):
   - Open baseline: Llama2-13B (quantized q4f16) — low-cost perf baseline
   - Higher-capacity open: Mistral-Instruct-7B-v2 — for instruction-following checks
   - Redwood-dedicated: rdw-8k-ensemble-v1 (proprietary optimized variant) — to measure parity delta
2) Acceptance thresholds (parity gating):
   - Intent recall >= 92% (measured on your 500-sample validation set)
   - False positive triage rate <= 4%
   - Regression budget vs. current baseline: no more than -2% absolute drop on accuracy metrics
3) Data & artifacts we need from you by Friday:
   - 500 labeled validation samples (CSV preferred) — see sample payload schema attached
   - 20 representative prompts covering table/log variants
   - Any redlines for PII/PHI handling you require
4) Deliverables from Redwood:
   - Benchmark report with per-model metrics (latency, tokens, accuracy, FP rate)
   - Prompt bundle + suggested prompt-engineering notes (we'll include control tokens for table inputs)
   - Meeting to review results and next-step recommendation at probe end

Links / attachments
- Prompt bundle: veridian_prompt_bundle_v1.json (attached)
- Sample payloads template: veridian_sample_payloads.csv (attached)
- Benchmark doc (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-veridian-benchmarks

Questions for you
- Do you have an existing labeled validation set or should we help bootstrap one from production logs?
- Any redlines on model families we should avoid for compliance (e.g., must be opt-in to open-source models)?

Next steps
- If that plan looks good I’ll open the trial, Marissa will set the evaluation pipeline, and Soojin will own parity gating and the report. Can we sync on Friday 10am PT to confirm data delivery?

Thanks — looking forward to running the probe.

—
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- We have ~1,200 historical triage interactions but only ~300 are labeled to our internal accuracy taxonomy. We can extract an additional 250 labeled samples by EOD Thursday; if needed we can work with you to label more.
- Compliance: we prefer not to use LLMs that persist data outside our VPC; open-source models are fine provided inference happens in our VPC (private deployment).
- Friday 10am PT works for a sync — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Jen

Karthik / Soojin / Jen — fyi on timeline and ops notes.

Trial run plan (high level) — 1 week perf & 1 week QA:
- Week 1 (throughput & latency): spin up 2xA100 equivalent nodes in Veridian VPC (we have an image for private deployment). Run continuous batching tests and p95 latency captures across the three model candidates.
- Week 2 (quality & parity): run the 800-sample validation (Jen’s 300 + 250 promised + 250 we can help label) across each model and produce the parity report.

Deliverables and owners:
- Infra & cost estimate (Marissa): I’ll prepare a ballpark for 2xA100 for 2 weeks incl. egress and storage. Preliminary: ~$13k–18k depending on utilization and the need for warm GPUs. Will send a tighter estimate by EOD.
- Eval harness (Soojin): I’ll hand the sample payload schema to you; we need to add table parsing tests (they mentioned 10–15% tables).
- Compliance checklist: We will run everything inside Veridian VPC and use customer-provided KMS for keys.

Quality concerns / regressions to watch for:
- Table extraction edge cases — open models often mis-handle semi-structured text, we should include prompt variations that explicitly annotate table boundaries.
- Hallucination on rare intents — add a small adversity set to measure hallucination rate (5–10% of tests).

Jen: if you can share the 250 additional labeled examples in the format attached (veridian_sample_payloads.csv) that will let us start the Week 2 tests immediately.

—
Marissa Cole

Thanks — quick technical notes from the evaluation side:

Acceptance gating (concrete metrics)
- Intent recall (micro-avg) >= 0.92 on the combined validation set (n >= 800)
- False positive triage rate <= 0.04 (95% CI)
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms (quantified on customer-shaped traffic with batching)
- Hallucination score <= 0.03 on adversity set (semantic hallucination measurement we run)

Benchmarks and what we’ll report
- Per-model confusion matrix, per-intent precision/recall, hallucination incidents with examples, latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), cost-per-1k-requests estimate.
- I’ll include prompt set variants and a short ablation showing if adding a explicit "TABLE_START/TABLE_END" token helps table parsing.

Operational ask for Veridian (what we need access to)
- SFTP or secure upload to their VPC endpoint for the validation CSV.
- A small sandbox dataset with live throughput pattern (a 12-hour sampling) so we can run realistic latency tests.

I’ll start the eval harness today once the sample CSV arrives. I’ll draft the parity report template and share before the Friday sync.

—
Soojin Lee
Evaluation Lead | Redwood Inference
